title: Q2 Roadmap / Launch Readiness + Incident Review
summary: Internal planning session to align Q2 roadmap priorities with launch readiness tasks and review a recent staging incident that caused a latency/regression blip. Decided immediate action items: run targeted load tests, update runbook, add a canary gating metric for p95 latency, and schedule a dry-run of the rollout next week.
next_steps: Alex to run focused load tests with the new batching/kv-cache config and share results by 2026-03-10
Samir to add p95 latency gating to canary job and test alerting by 2026-03-09
Maria to finalize release checklist and stakeholder notification plan by 2026-03-08
Priya to own the dry-run coordination and invite cross-functional reps for 2026-03-12
Taylor to update QA smoke tests and schedule extended soak run with dataset v3 by 2026-03-11
action_items: Alex Chen: run load tests (batching + kv-cache) and post results in #prod-infra by 2026-03-10
Samir Patel: implement p95 gating in canary pipeline; validate alerts by 2026-03-09
Maria Lopez: update release checklist and runbook edits; circulate for review by 2026-03-08
Taylor Rivers: extend QA smoke tests and run soak for 2 hours; report anomalies by 2026-03-11
Priya Natarajan: schedule dry-run and confirm attendees; prepare dry-run agenda by 2026-03-12
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 14:30 UTC | Duration: 1h15m | Attendees: Priya, Alex, Samir, Maria, Taylor

Priya (00:00): ok good afternoon everyone, sorry running a tiny bit late, i had a convo with legal about the private deploy notes, but let's kick off. agenda is q2 roadmap items that touch launch readiness, and then a short postmortem from the staging incident on tuesday.

Alex (00:22): yeah, i'll start with the incident summary quickly, uh, so on staging we saw a p95 spike up to ~1.2s from our usual 700ms after the change that enabled continuous batching + small kv-cache tweak. it was intermitt— intermittent and seemed to correlate with long sequences from the eval harness.

Samir (00:47): adding — adding to that, some of the instances came up with larger GC pauses, which i think is the java lib mismatch but we need to confirm. there was also a small tput drop when autoscaler decided to scale down prematurely.

Maria (01:10): do we know if it was the kernel selection change in the new build? alex, you pushed a kernel update, right?

Alex (01:18): yes i did a minor kernel selector tweak to prefer the fused_attention path for sequences > 512; i suspect that for certain shorter sequences it still selected a suboptimal kernel due to seq length misclassification in the prepass. also the batching heuristic boundaries might've caused large batch formation and a p95 regression when a few long requests entered the same batch.

Taylor (01:45): QA saw it too — our smoke caught increased latency but it was flakey, sometimes pass sometimes fail, it's hard to reproduce locally. the transcripts had some tokenization differences too, not sure if that matters.

Priya (02:05): ok action oriented: we need to decide whether to roll back the kernel change on prod candidate, or put a canary gating in place. prefer gating. we can't rollback every perf improvement.

Alex (02:20): agree gating. we should add a p95 p99 threshold as canary gates and also add a metric for batch-size distribution so we can detect when we form unusually large batches.

Samir (02:35): i'll add the p95 gate to the canary job; quick question: what's the threshold? previous baseline was p95 800ms for the workload; we had a target of 750ms for q2.

Priya (02:48): let's be pragmatic: gate at 900ms p95 for the canary, with a loud alert. if canary breaches twice in a 10 minute window rollback. we can refine after the dry-run.

Maria (03:05): and for launch readiness checklist specifics — we still have outstanding items: docs updated, runbook updated with the incident flow, legal signoff for private deployment notes, and load-test results. who owns docs?

Priya (03:20): Maria will own the checklist and docs circulation. alex will deliver load tests. samir will update canary pipeline. taylor will extend QA soak.

Taylor (03:33): noted. for QA soak, i want to run the negative path tests too — e.g., KV cache miss storms and prefix cache pressure tests. will need a small dataset that simulates short+long sequence mix. alex can you share that sample?

Alex (03:48): yes, i have a trimmed harness dataset v3 that mirrors production seq distribution, will push to shared drive. small caveat, it includes some PII-like tokens but it's synthetic.

Samir (04:05): on autoscaler, we observed scale-down when bursty traffic ended but the pending batch queue still had inflight KV merges, led to transient queuing. i propose we add a scale-down cooldown of 120s for model servers until the batch queue drains.

Alex (04:26): good call. i'll implement a cooldown param; quick patch should be low risk.

Priya (04:36): excellent. also, we're pressing on rollout timing: q2 launch window target is 2026-03-20 for beta customers. we need a dry-run the week before — that is 2026-03-12. can everyone make that?

All (04:51): yes / ok / noted / i'll be there.

Maria (05:00): a couple of roadmap asks: product wants quant recommendations surfaced in the console by end of q2, and optimize team needs a prioritization on model variants to support for public launch. this is separate but we should slot a follow-up.

Priya (05:20): yes add an item — product + optimize sync next week.

(05:30) [Side conversation — Priya & Maria about stakeholder invite list; brief crosstalk, unclear transcription]

Alex (06:10): running through the technical items: kernel rollback is option B, option A is canary gating + batch-size histogram + cooldown. cost impact of gating is minimal but we need to capture the metrics. implement in staging, run repeated 2-hour soak, validate.

Samir (06:40): i'll also add logging for GC pause distribution to help analyze the suspected java lib issue. if pauses >200ms occur more than 5 times in 10 minutes we'll create an incident ticket.

Taylor (06:58): QA will validate the new logs and make sure they correlate with the perf alerts; also, i'll add a smoke test that sends mixed seq-length requests to verify kernel selection decision path.

Priya (07:20): great. let's capture owner+due dates here — alex tests and posts results by 2026-03-10; samir implements canary gating by 2026-03-09; maria to finalize checklist 2026-03-08; taylor soak by 2026-03-11.

Alex (07:40): one more note on batching: i think the heuristic should cap batch size at 64 for now; that avoids pathological large batch formation for mixed sequences. we can revisit after more data.

Samir (07:54): agreed cap 64, and we will surface the percent of batches near cap. that metric will go to dashboards.

Priya (08:06): good. communication plan: Maria will send the stakeholder note after checklist is done; Priya will handle exec update if dry-run shows issues.

Maria (08:20): on legal/privacy docs: i have a short outstanding question from security about KMS rotation for private deployments; i'll follow up with security and loop back.

Priya (08:33): ok. any other risks?

Alex (08:36): risk is mainly perf regressions we can't reproduce locally; mitigate by improving harness fidelity and adding more telemetry in the runtime. Also model quant noise for certain layers — not likely for this change but flagging.

Taylor (08:52): from QA perspective, dependent services stubbing is flaky in our current harness; will work with infra to stabilize.

Samir (09:04): note: we should also verify autoscaler behaviour under pod pre-emption scenarios (cloud provider might preempt GPUs). add as a test case.

Priya (09:20): excellent. quick recap — decisions made: do not rollback, implement canary gating and batch cap=64, add cooldown on scale-down 120s, add p95 gating at 900ms, run 2-hour soaking tests, and schedule dry-run 2026-03-12. owners assigned as in action items.

Alex (09:46): i'll push a PR with the batch cap and the kernel selection fallback and mention the canary gate changes. will tag samir for the pipeline changes.

Samir (10:00): i'll instrument the canary pipeline tonight and validate alerting tomorrow morning.

Taylor (10:08): QA will begin the extended soak on staging after alex posts the harness and samir flips the canary gate to staging.

Maria (10:18): i'll send the stakeholder note and the release checklist by monday.

Priya (10:26): perfect. anything else?

(10:30) [short silence, some typing noises in background]

Priya (10:40): thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

End transcript. Notes: transcription contains small errors and some speaker overlaps; replaced speaker surnames with first names for readability.
